title: Low-Frequency Charge Noise in Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Jessica Richter, Max J. Ruckriegel, Jonas D. Gerber, Tijl Degroote, Christoph Adam, Markus Niese, Lara Ostertag, Clara Galante, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Petar Tomic, Artem O. Denisov, Hadrien Duprez, Klaus Ensslin, Thomas Ihn
abstract: Bilayer graphene (BLG) quantum dots (QDs) are a promising platform for semiconductor qubits. However, the low-frequency charge noise that may ultimately limit coherence has remained largely unexplored. Here, we systematically characterize charge noise in gate-defined BLG QDs using transport-based noise spectroscopy. We extract a median amplitude of $ S_μ^{1/2} (1~\text{Hz}) = 1.16~μ\text{eV}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, placing BLG well within the range reported for established semiconductor quantum-dot platforms. Across variations in charge occupation, confinement, source-drain bias, and charge-sensor operating conditions, neither the noise amplitude nor the spectral dependence shows a reproducible trend in electrostatic tuning, indicating that we extracted the intrinsic semiconductor noise. Consistent noise levels are further observed in double QDs and confirmed using an independent superconducting resonator-based dispersive readout. Extending the study to BLG devices incorporating transition metal dichalcogenide layers reveals no measurable charge noise increase in weakly proximitized QDs. These results validate BLG as a viable platform for coherent quantum information processing.
summary: This experimental work characterizes the low-frequency charge noise in Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots using noise spectroscopy. The measured noise levels are competitive with established semiconductor platforms, and the noise proves robust against systematic electrostatic tuning. These results strongly validate BLG as a promising material for developing coherent solid-state qubits.
main_problem: The study aimed to characterize and assess the low-frequency charge noise in Bilayer Graphene (BLG) Quantum Dots (QDs) to determine if the material is a viable platform for coherent quantum information processing.
main_result: The measured charge noise amplitude ($1.16 \mu	ext{eV}/\sqrt{	ext{Hz}}$) places BLG within the range of established semiconductor platforms, and the noise levels showed no systematic dependence on varying electrostatic tuning parameters.
method: The noise was characterized using transport-based noise spectroscopy by observing current fluctuations at the flank of a Coulomb blockade resonance, with independent confirmation via superconducting resonator readout.
model_or_system: The physical system is gate-defined BLG QDs, sometimes extended to incorporate Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD) layers, fabricated in a van-der-Waals heterostructure.
key_observables: Median charge-noise amplitude ($S_{1/2\mu}(1 	ext{ Hz})$), Power Spectral Density (PSD) $S_\mu(f)$, and integrated charge noise ($\sigma_\mu$).
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperature (20 mK), charge occupation, confinement potential, source-drain bias ($|V_{SD}|$), and sensor operating power.
main_assumptions: The noise is attributed to Two-Level Fluctuators (TLFs) in dielectrics or interfaces, and the lack of systematic dependence suggests the noise is intrinsic to the environment rather than the gate-tunable parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the device heterostructure and measurement procedure. Figure 2 compares the extracted charge noise amplitudes of BLG to other QD platforms. Figure 3 demonstrates the lack of systematic evolution of noise parameters when varying electrostatic tuning parameters.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes charge noise by varying multiple operational parameters (occupation, bias, confinement) using transport spectroscopy, confirms results with an independent readout method, and extends the study to hybrid TMD/BLG systems.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses the primary decoherence mechanism (charge noise) limiting qubit coherence, providing quantitative metrics essential for assessing any solid-state platform for quantum computation.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
